The Garber story

From a popcorn stand to 25 dealerships.

The Garber Automotive Group story starts on the outskirts of Lansing on a small farm, where Guy S. Garber was born in 1884. Guy was homeschooled his whole life by his mother, and the family was so poor, they couldn’t afford shoes for him in the winter. But these humble beginnings couldn’t hold Guy’s entrepreneurial skills back. At only nine years old, he started his first business selling popcorn in Lansing. He took the work ethic and skills he built from that job to selling newspapers as a teenager, and to eventually working alongside his father to sell farm implements.

Guy Garber’s work ethic and sales prowess caught the eye of Billy Durant, one of the founders of General Motors. In 1907, Durant invited the 23-year-old Guy Garber to Flint to work for Buick. Three years later, Garber arrived in Saginaw and opened the store that would eventually become Garber Buick, our flagship store. In 1912, he bought out Buick’s interest in the Saginaw Valley region and by 1913, Garber was one of the original Buick Thirteen distributors.

He held that Buick distributorship until his death in 1965. But that wasn’t the end of the Garber story. His son, Richard Garber Sr., took over and guided the store through the 1960s. And in 1980, Guy’s grandson Richard J. Garber Jr. became president in the company’s 73rd year, making him the youngest Buick dealer in the nation.

Garber Automotive Group has grown significantly since Guy first opened shop in 1907. Today, the organization includes 25 new-vehicle dealerships representing 16 brands across six states. We also are home to RightWay Auto Sales, a chain of used car dealerships; Gateway Financial Solutions, a subprime lending company; and the Saginaw Spirit, an OHL hockey franchise who are the 2024 Memorial Cup champions. All this and more while still being owned by the same family that started it all over a hundred years ago.

1965 – Today

Three generations at the wheel.

Every leader of Garber Automotive Group has been family, and they’ve all carried the same belief of supporting the community that supports them. Guy founded the Saginaw Society for Crippled Children; his son Richard raised money to help renovate the YMCA; and his grandson Richard J. Garber Jr. has led campaigns to support the United Way, the CAN Council, and the Temple Theater.

1907 – 1965

Guy S. Garber

Founder. One of the Buick Thirteen, first president of the Michigan Automobile Dealers Association, and a civic leader who made service to Saginaw the priority of his life.

1965 – 1972

Richard Garber Sr.

Second generation. President and owner until 1972; Jaycees' Outstanding Young Man, Arnold Boutell Award for community service, Saginaw YMCA board president.

1980 – Present

Richard J. Garber Jr.

Third generation. President since 1980 and the builder of Garber Automotive Group who calls himself the steward of his grandfather’s business. He has been on the board of directors for numerous charitable and community organizations within Saginaw County.

Our History

A century of automotive pioneering.

In 1907, most of Michigan still thought the horse and buggy were here to stay. Guy S. Garber, a 23-year-old farm-implement salesman, had a different vision – one where the automobile was the future of transportation. His passion caught the eye of Billy Durant, the founder of General Motors, who put him on the road to selling Buicks and opening dealerships across Michigan.

Guy Garber opened a Buick dealership in Saginaw in 1910, bought out the factory’s retail interest in 1912, and by 1913, he held the wholesale territory from Saginaw County all the way north to the Straits of Mackinac. His partnership with GM lasted nearly 60 years, and when he died in 1965, Garber Buick was the last Buick distributor in America.

Where the name first went over a door: R. J. Garber Farm Implements, 414 N. Washington Avenue, Lansing.

Guy Garber at work in the Saginaw office.

1907

Guy S. Garber goes to work for Buick

At William C. Durant's urging, the 23-year-old salesman becomes a Buick representative and opens a dealership in Battle Creek.

1912

Garber Buick is born

Buick leaves the retail business; Guy buys its Saginaw Valley interest. A year later, he is sole owner and one of the Buick Thirteen distributors.

1965

Guy Garber Passes Away at 81

After 58 years working in the auto industry, Guy Garber passes away at 81. Richard Garber Sr., his son, takes over as president and owner of Garber Buick.

1980

Richard J. Garber Jr.

Richard J. Garber Jr., Guy Garber's grandson, becomes president in the company's 73rd year, making him the youngest Buick dealer in the nation.

1986

One store becomes a group

Garber Automotive Group is born. Garber Nissan in Saginaw, Michigan and Garber Ford in Green Cove Springs, Florida are the first acquisitions.

New state · Florida
1996

RightWay Auto Sales and Gateway Financial Solutions

Garber Automotive Group establishes RightWay Auto Sales, a chain of used-car dealerships, and Gateway Financial Solutions, a subprime lending agency.

1997

Glendale Heights, Illinois

Garber adds Sunrise Chevrolet in Glendale Heights, Illinois. It is the group’s third state and first venture into the Chicago Metro area.

New state · Illinois
2002

The Saginaw Spirit come to the Great Lakes Bay Region

Garber brings the Saginaw Spirit, an OHL franchise, to the Dow Event Center. They eventually become the 2024 Memorial Cup champions.

2011

Rochester, New York

Acura, Honda, Porsche and Audi franchise dealerships based in Rochester, New York join Garber Automotive Group, expanding the group into four states.

New state · New York
2018–19

Hilton Head, South Carolina and Highland, Indiana

Two new dealerships are brought under the Garber umbrella, adding two states in two years – a Buick GMC Cadillac store in Bluffton, SC, and a Chevrolet store in Highland, IN.

New state · South CarolinaNew state · Indiana
